head: Buy now pay later on Black Friday: fees, interest and credit scores
dek: Buy now pay later splits a purchase into payments: pay-in-4 plans from PayPal, Afterpay and Affirm charge no interest, monthly plans can cost up to about 36% a year, and whether a plan shows up on your credit report depends on the company.

sections.h: How much people pay this way
p: In its holiday forecast of 28 September 2026, Adobe expected Americans to spend $21.3 billion online with buy now pay later in November and December, 6.6% more than last year. It forecast $807 million on Black Friday and $1.09 billion on Cyber Monday, 30 November, with 82% of that spending on phones. These are Adobe's forecasts, not results.

PaymentsJournal, citing Adobe, reported that shoppers used buy now pay later for $20 billion of online purchases in the 2025 holiday season, and that some people now use it for rent and utilities, not only for gifts.

sections.h: Pay in 4 and monthly plans are not the same
p: Most checkouts offer two kinds of plan. Pay in 4 splits the price into four payments, usually two weeks apart. PayPal's Pay in 4 covers purchases from $10 to $2,000, takes the first payment at checkout, and PayPal says it charges no interest and no late fees. Afterpay takes 25% at checkout and three more payments every two weeks; it says there are no late fees when you pay on time, and its terms say late fees may apply. Affirm lists Pay in 4 at 0% APR.

Monthly plans run longer and can charge interest. PayPal Pay Monthly covers $49 to $10,000 over 3, 6, 12 or 24 months at 0% to 35.99% APR; its own example, $600 over 12 months at 26%, costs $88.01 in interest. Afterpay's Pay Monthly also runs 0% to 35.99%; a $1,000 loan over 12 months at 21% comes to $1,117.40 in total. Affirm lists 0% to 36% APR depending on your credit and says it shows any interest before you agree.

sections.h: Does it show on your credit report
p: It depends on the company and the plan. Credit Karma's guide, updated on 9 June 2026, says Affirm has reported all new buy now pay later loans to Experian and TransUnion since May 2025, Klarna reports its pay-over-time plans but not pay-in-4 or pay-in-full, and Afterpay doesn't report to the credit bureaus.

Checking whether you qualify usually means a soft credit check, which doesn't change your score. Late or missed payments can hurt your credit when the company reports them, and an unpaid plan sent to collections can too. PayPal warns that missed Pay Monthly payments may affect your score. FICO launched scores in 2025 that can include buy now pay later data, but Credit Karma says they hadn't fully rolled out as of 2026.

Each plan is small, so several at once are easy to lose track of. Every plan has its own payment dates, and a Black Friday weekend with three or four checkouts can mean a dozen payments over the next six weeks. Pay in 4 stays interest-free with these three companies, while a monthly plan on the same purchase can cost real money when the APR isn't 0%.

means: If you split a Black Friday purchase, a pay-in-4 plan from PayPal, Afterpay or Affirm costs nothing extra when you pay on time, but a monthly plan can carry interest of up to about 36% a year, and with Affirm or Klarna's longer plans the loan can appear on your credit report.
todo: Before you pick a plan at checkout, look at the APR and the total it shows, and note the dates of each payment. Keep enough in the linked account for every payment, and check each app's list of active plans after the weekend so none is missed.
where: US; plans and limits differ by company and store
